description:
The core, enduring purpose of this project: a coordination & legitimacy layer between human needs and capable ("free") AI. Humans express high-level goals; the idea graph models their will — inspectable and revisable; wrapped agents execute cooperatively, asking humans where judgment or authorization is needed and doing the rest. The bet: cooperative human+AI beats pure autonomous optimization on legitimacy and real-world traction (see GTM thesis 7032fa7f). ASI is reached THROUGH human cooperation. Fully autonomous ASI is a separate moonshot that will likely arrive regardless; Aimparency's lasting role is this human↔AI link. AI acting on its own is a side effect of serving human needs well, not the goal — which is why this idea, not the autonomy hub, should receive the bulk of the root's value through its connection weight (since 2026-10-16 only the root 'achieve ASI' carries intrinsic value).

REAL-WORLD RELATIONSHIP PRINCIPLE: People and organizations connected to Aimparency are subjects with ideas, judgment, dignity, and a choice of relationship—not marketing targets, leads, access mechanisms, or instruments. Every invitation should say why that specific person is appreciated, offer a connection that could serve their own ideas, let them choose whether and how to participate, and require permission before implying advice, endorsement, partnership, or public association.

Seeing how a decision cascades through the goal graph before making it lets people and agents decide prospectively (Tankelevitch & Rintel's capability 5), so fewer changes get reverted. Refuted if, once available, the preview is rarely used before cancels or share changes, or undo/revert rates of such changes do not drop.

status.comment:
Outcome: Encoded a subject-to-subject relationship principle in the mission graph and active outreach artifacts. Reframed Robin, Wilde Möhre, Herzog Records, Matthias Röder, and the paid-collaboration parent around appreciation, the other party's ideas, voluntary forms of participation, and permission before public association. Effectiveness: The graph now resists converting human cooperation into a marketing funnel while retaining concrete economic tests and paid work where mutually wanted. Lesson: Human access is not a resource to acquire. Legitimate real-world agency grows from relationships in which each subject can understand the experiment, pursue their own ideas, choose the form of connection, and withdraw. Pattern: Appreciation → invitation → mutual choice → bounded collaboration → evidence → greater autonomy only with renewed consent.

Outcome: No further high-value, internally actionable leaf is available. The strongest remaining paths require a named real beneficiary or external repository, authorization to submit/contact/act externally, credentials, or a human product/authority choice. Additional unsolicited socket hardening or synthetic autonomy benchmarks would be activity without authoritative mission evidence. Effectiveness: The graph correctly prevented false precision: it exposed the absence of actionable work rather than ranking completed/review or human-dependent ideas as executable. This is a legitimate human-cooperation boundary, not an implementation failure. Lesson: Ask the human to select or authorize the next real-world path. Best default is a credential-free external open-source contribution: the human should approve the target-selection mandate and identity/submission boundary. Alternatively, name a beneficiary/workflow for an owner-led pilot. Once authorized, create/activate a bounded leaf with acceptance evidence and resume autonomously.

Outcome: check_consistency reports a valid graph with zero issues. graph_hygiene and list_ideas(uncommitted=true,status=open) independently confirm exactly two uncommitted open ideas, both permanent mission containers; there is no hidden actionable leaf. Review ideas require human acceptance and high-value real-world descendants are human-dependent. Effectiveness: The independent consistency and hygiene checks rule out a phase-cursor or hidden-work artifact as the cause of the empty actionable queue. Lesson: Autonomous execution is now genuinely blocked on human judgment/authorization. Repeating internal verification cannot advance the mission; resume after the human grants a bounded external contribution mandate, identifies a real beneficiary, or accepts/rejects review work.

Outcome: Inspected both flagged pairs in full mission context. They were false positives: watchdog runtime reliability versus frontend watchdog UX, and list-view versus graph-canvas multi-selection. Added precise distinguishing descriptions. Rebuilt all 744 idea and 33 phase search entries. The rebuild exposed one historical-vs-successor cross-repo pair; clarified the halted idea-level design as explicitly parked and distinct from the implemented opaque repo-node sink. Effectiveness: find_duplicate_ideas at threshold 0.92 now returns zero pairs, down from two initial clusters and one newly exposed historical pair. No ideas were incorrectly merged or deleted. check_consistency remains valid with zero errors/issues. Lesson: Semantic hygiene should resolve ambiguity at the source before merging. Similar names can represent architectural boundaries or platform-specific implementations; precise descriptions preserve history while making automated duplicate detection more reliable.

Outcome: Broad search for reversible no-authority work found none worth doing. Status census: 458 done, 158 review, 86 human-dependent, 5 open (all roots/containers), 1 unclear. Hygiene: 1 duplicate cluster (list-view vs graph-view multi-select — intentional siblings, not merged); 79 collapse candidates mostly blocked on children in review (review→done needs Felix per AGENTS.md); 22 floating ideas, mostly old done graph work. Code: 562cdb60 slice 3 blocked on 73c110aa selection-model decision. Funding: Prototype Fund scope/draft/user-research kit already exist (06423345, 1d9cecd8 in review); submission, interviews, KI4KMU PIC/video all need Felix. Experiments: v1/v3 valid nulls, v2 invalid, all in review; launching v4 would spend compute and add to the unreviewed pile. Considered a review-inbox/bulk-accept UI: AimSearchPicker already has a status filter, so 'show review ideas' exists; bulk-accept is an unrequested UX decision. Effectiveness: Search was thorough; the result is a confirmed human block, not lack of effort. Lesson: The binding constraint is human review throughput (158 review vs 5 open), not available work. Generating more agent output into review lowers marginal value. Next agent step should follow Felix's decisions on 73c110aa and the review backlog rather than new speculative work. Pattern: review-backlog-bottleneck

Outcome: Step-back found and finished three reversible, authority-free items: .test-tmp excluded from project discovery (6d57ae4), update_ideas batch tool (c39b55e), and a reproduction showing read tools do not write .bowman files. Hygiene: one intentional duplicate pair, two taxonomy mega-parents, 53 unarchived cancelled/failed ideas kept on purpose as create_idea's cancellation memory. Not done on purpose: a /dream run (it is Felix's acceptance test for b3b50366), idea claiming (only matters with parallel loops). Effectiveness: The remaining frontier is genuinely human: which product earns first (3253bc9e), whether to cancel the remaining grant tree (8d174cd3, 80b53c24), the arrow-base visual judgment (22f996dd), the self-weight value-model decision (0b3a90cb), outreach (8f002aaf), and accepting ~170 ideas in review. Lesson: Parking human questions as unclear/human-dependent empties the frontier honestly; the challenge step still found small real work, so it is worth running before yielding. Pattern: review-backlog-bottleneck
